# Ensemble Room — Low-Cost Multi-Agent Runtime for OpenCode

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/ensemble-room-lowcost.svg?color=cb3837&style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ensemble-room-lowcost)
[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/ensemble-room-lowcost.svg?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ensemble-room-lowcost)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.23-339933.svg?style=flat-square)](https://nodejs.org)

**A hardened, token-efficient multi-agent orchestration runtime for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai).**

`ensemble-room-lowcost` gives you a shared team room — an orchestrator (lead), specialists, an SDET and a
quality-gate reviewer — running on top of OpenCode, with a SQLite-backed task board, per-agent model
fallback and a deterministic test suite. It is derived from `@hueyexe/opencode-ensemble@0.18.0` and
hardened in the `0.18.x` line around one single objective: **do the same orchestration while burning far
fewer tokens**.

The two structural wins:

- **Teammates are born in standby** — spawning a worker costs **zero tokens**; the first real message is
  what wakes it, exactly once.
- **The lead rests in absolute silence** — lead-bound messages accumulate in SQLite (`delivered = 0`) and
  are injected on the lead's next legitimate turn. The only automatic wake is a **single deterministic
  event: total board closure**.

## 1. Why this runtime

Multi-agent systems are expensive for a structural reason: **every coordination event is a model turn**.
A naive room wakes the orchestrator on every teammate message, wakes teammates the moment they are
created, and mistakes a compacting session for a dead one. Tokens are spent on plumbing instead of on
work.

This runtime removes the plumbing cost at its source:

| Cost driver | Naive behaviour | This runtime |
|---|---|---|
| Spawning a teammate | init prompt is sent immediately | `standby: true` → session registered, **prompt deferred**, 0 tokens |
| Teammate wake-up | any message, any time | first message is the wake, guarded by an **idempotent single-consumer transition** |
| Lead wake-up | one `promptAsync` per `team_message` | messages persist in SQLite; lead is woken **only** by board closure |
| Long/compacting sessions | aborted as stale by the TTL watchdog | **compaction immunity** + active progress heartbeat |
| Rate-limited model | every request retries the same model | per-agent **fallback chain** with burst de-duplication |
| Schema drift | `CHECK` constraint rejects new states | **idempotent rebuild migrations** carrying every column |

The design rule behind all of it: **state lives in the schema, not in conventions.** A lifecycle
transition is a guarded `UPDATE … WHERE execution_status = …`, so two concurrent actors can never both
consume the same wake.

---

### 2.1 Data flow of a wake

```text
producer                    SQLite                       consumer
────────                    ──────                       ────────
team_message(to: B) ──▶ team_message row (delivered=0)
                           │
                           ├─ B.execution_status == 'standby'
                           │     └─ UPDATE … WHERE execution_status='standby'
                           │            → 'starting'
                           │            → promptAsync( spawn_context + text )
                           │
                           └─ B.execution_status != 'standby'
                                 └─ promptAsync( text )

team_message(to: lead) ──▶ team_message row (delivered=0)
                           └─ silentLead=true → NO promptAsync
                                 lead's next legal turn:
                                 buildLeadSystemPrompt() injects backlog
                                 → delivered = 1

team_tasks_complete ─────▶ completed === total
                           └─ exactly 1× promptAsync to lead
                              [System: All team tasks completed on board by <who>]
```

### 2.2 Event model

1. **One wake channel per role.** For teammates, `promptAsync` is the transport. For the lead under
   `silentLead: true`, the **SQLite row is the delivery** and the system prompt is the renderer.
2. **Guarded transitions.** Every lifecycle change is an `UPDATE … WHERE` on the previous state, which
   makes the wake idempotent by construction.
3. **No polling loops.** The lead wake is strictly event-driven (board closure). The watchdog is a
   single TTL-guarded tick, not an agent-driven scan.
4. **Roles are enforced by the schema.** The SDET executes deterministic tests but cannot approve a
   card; only the quality-gate reviewer (or the lead) can complete it.

---

## 3. The five hardening layers

Each layer below is a fix for a concrete failure mode, shipped with its own deterministic suite.

### 3.1 Native Standby — zero tokens at spawn, idempotent wake

**Failure mode.** In the upstream model, `team_spawn` sends the init prompt when the session is created.
Every teammate burns tokens the instant it is born, before any work exists for it.

**Implementation** (`src/tools/team-spawn.ts`, `team-message.ts`, `team-broadcast.ts`):

- `standby: true` registers the member **without** sending any prompt. The session is created with
  `execution_status = 'standby'` and the full prompt is persisted in `team_member.spawn_context`
  (Migration 11).
- The **first** `team_message` / `team_broadcast` addressed to that member is the waker: the delivered
  text has `spawn_context` **prepended**, and the transition `standby → starting` happens through
  `UPDATE … WHERE execution_status = 'standby'`. That predicate is the **one-consumer guard**: two
  simultaneous messages cannot both deliver the init.
- **Fail-safe.** If the wake `promptAsync` throws, the hook restores `execution_status = 'standby'` so a
  retry — or the undelivered-message recovery pass — replays the full `spawn_context` instead of an
  empty prompt.
- **No lost messages.** Messages that arrive before the wake stay queued and join the same turn.

**Guarantee:** `tests/test_standby_lifecycle.mjs` — born in standby with no prompt, wake exactly once,
revert on transport failure, `retry_until` attempts completing `standby → starting`.

### 3.2 Migration 12 — schema rebuild with the `standby` literal

**Failure mode.** `team_member.execution_status` is a SQLite `CHECK` constraint with fixed literals.
SQLite **cannot `ALTER` a `CHECK`**. A database created from scratch would reject the standby `INSERT`
with a constraint error, while a long-lived database only worked because it predated the constraint.

**Implementation** (`src/schema.ts`, Migration 12):

- Rebuild in the pattern already consolidated by Migrations 8 and 13:
  `RENAME → CREATE → INSERT … SELECT → DROP`, then **recreate both indexes** that die with the old
  table (`team_member_session_idx`, `team_member_status_idx`).
- The new table carries **every** column added between Migrations 3 and 11 — `worktree_dir`,
  `worktree_branch`, `plan_approval`, `workspace_id`, `reported_to_lead`, `last_nudged_at`,
  `retry_until`, `retry_attempt`, `retry_provider`, `retry_message`, `spawn_context` — so the rebuild is
  lossless.
- The new `CHECK` accepts `standby` alongside the pre-existing literals
  (`idle, starting, running, cancel_requested, cancelling, cancelled, completing, completed, failed,
  timed_out, standby`).
- `applyMigrations()` runs each migration inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE … COMMIT` under
  `PRAGMA user_version`, with `foreign_keys` saved and restored. The upgrade path is therefore
  **atomic and idempotent**: a legacy database and a fresh bootstrap converge on the same schema.
- If the stored version is newer than the bundle supports, the runtime throws an explicit
  "upgrade the plugin" error instead of corrupting data.

**Guarantee:** the suites apply the real `MIGRATIONS` array to a real SQLite database — both fresh and
upgrade-from-legacy — and assert `src ↔ dist` parity.

### 3.3 Hook Shielding — no false alarms, no spurious nudges

**Failure mode.** Two independent triggers were blind to standby and to legitimately blocked work:

1. the idle **nudge** would send a prompt to a freshly created member that should never have received one;
2. the `fast-idle` **alarm** would announce "the agent died" for someone legitimately parked.

**Implementation** (`src/hooks.ts`, exported through `src/index.ts`):

- `shouldNudgeIdleMember(db, teamId, member)` returns `false` when `execution_status === 'standby'`
  (in addition to the already-covered blocked states), and still honours the `last_nudged_at` window.
- `shouldAlarmFastIdle(...)` returns `false` for `standby`, preserving the alarm only for genuine idle.
  The predicate was extracted from the bundle's inline block into a testable seam **without changing the
  decision**.
- `hasBlockedAssignedTasks(...)` keeps legitimately blocked work visible to the team nudge without
  producing an alarm.

**Guarantee:** `tests/test_standby_lifecycle.mjs` asserts **zero false `fast-idle` alarms** across the
whole suite (check `D12`) and exercises nudge and wake concurrently.

### 3.4 Resilient Watchdog — active heartbeat and compaction immunity

**Failure mode.** The watchdog tears sessions down on a TTL (`stallThresholdMs`, default 300 s). A
session in **context compaction** does not advance `time_updated`, so it was aborted as "stale" — an
undue timeout that destroyed context and forced expensive rework.

**Implementation** (`src/watchdog.ts`, `src/progress.ts`):

- **Active heartbeat.** On each check, a stale member whose session shows real progress
  (`ProgressTracker`: new steps / output tokens above `stallTokenThreshold` after `stallMinSteps`) gets
  `time_updated` **renewed** and keeps running (`watchdog:heartbeat:renewed`).
- **Compaction immunity.** `isSessionCompacting(sessionId)` reads `session.time_compacting` from the
  host session store **read-only**. When the value is `> 0`, the session is not aborted on this tick and
  is re-evaluated on the next (`watchdog:heartbeat:compacting`).
- A compaction value of `0` does **not** buy immunity — the race is decided correctly. Genuinely idle
  sessions still transition to `error / timed_out`, with a lead warning, a toast and worktree cleanup.
- `stallThresholdMs = 0` disables the TTL while keeping worktree GC. A missing or corrupted store
  returns `false` without throwing.
- `start()` wraps `check()` in a logged `.catch` and `unref()`s both timers; `dispose()` is idempotent
  and `stop()` remains a legacy alias.

**Guarantee:** `tests/test_watchdog_heartbeat.mjs` — four scenarios (active, compacting, idle,
compaction = 0) executed **against both `dist` and `src`**, materializing the `session` store from the
versioned DDL in `tests/fixtures/session_schema.sql` (no dependency on the host database).

## 8. Troubleshooting

### The lead never wakes up

Expected when `silentLead: true` (the default): lead-bound messages only appear in the lead's **next**
turn, and the single automatic wake is total board closure. Check the board state:

```text
team_tasks_list()
```

If `completed < total`, no wake will fire by design. Team status and task state are also visible in the
dashboard (`http://127.0.0.1:4747`). To restore per-message wakes, set `"silentLead": false`.

### A teammate spawns but never does anything

That is **native standby working**. The session is created with `execution_status = 'standby'` and the
prompt is stored in `spawn_context` (zero tokens spent). Send the first `team_message` — it is the
waker. If the wake transport fails, the runtime reverts the member to `standby`, so simply retry.

### `SQLite constraint failed: CHECK constraint failed: team_member`

The database predates Migration 12 and was not rebuilt. OpenCode must boot the current bundle **once**
against that database; `applyMigrations()` performs the `RENAME → CREATE → COPY → DROP` rebuild
atomically. Verify the bundle is the one actually loaded (`dist/index.js` mtime) and restart OpenCode.

### `Database schema version N is newer than this plugin supports (M)`

The database was written by a newer plugin version. Upgrade the package; do not downgrade by hand, and do
not edit `PRAGMA user_version` — the column set would no longer match the `CHECK` constraints.

### A long session is killed after five minutes

- Confirm `stallThresholdMs` (default `300000`). Set `0` to disable the TTL entirely (worktree GC stays
  active).
- Compaction immunity only applies while the host store reports `session.time_compacting > 0`. A
  corrupted or missing store intentionally returns `false` (fail-fast) instead of masking a real stall.
- Sessions that show real progress are renewed by the heartbeat; a session making no steps and no tokens
  is genuinely stalled.

### Failover does not switch models

Check, in order:

1. **Format.** Chain entries must be `provider/model` or `provider/model#variant`. `#default` is the
   server's absence marker and is normalized away — it will never match a chain entry.
2. **Scope.** The member's agent key must exist in `fallbackModelsByAgent`, or the global
   `fallbackModels` / `modelFallback` applies. The global chain **never** hijacks isolated or lead
   sessions; those require an explicit per-agent chain.
3. **Cooldown.** `FAILOVER_COOLDOWN_MS` (10 min per `teamId:memberName`) intentionally collapses a burst
   into one advance. A second distinct 429 inside the window is suppressed.
4. **Exhaustion.** If the current model is already the last chain entry, the decision is `exhausted`:
   only a log entry and the cooldown are produced, with no lead notification and no further switches.
   The lead is woken exclusively by the systematic full-board closure event — failover never wakes it.

### Dashboard port is busy, or the dashboard does not answer

`dashboardPort` defaults to `4747`. Set another port, or `0` to disable. The server binds `127.0.0.1`
only and rejects requests whose `Host`/`Origin` do not match — behind a reverse proxy, preserve the
original `Host` header. Verify the runtime is live with `curl http://127.0.0.1:4747/api/health`.

### `npm test` fails immediately with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`

Dependencies are not installed. Run `npm ci` (or `npm install`) in the repository root first. The
suites import real packages by design — there are no stubs to fall back on.

### Type errors during `npm run typecheck`

The compiler settings live in `tsconfig.json`; `typescript` is a devDependency. Run `npm ci` to
restore the exact locked version. The published runtime is the pre-built `dist/index.js`, so a local
type error never affects a consumer — but it does gate contributions.

### `npm run build` produces a bundle the host rejects

Build with the pinned command:

```bash
npm run build   # esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --packages=external
```

`--packages=external` keeps `@opencode-ai/*`, `solid-js`, `@opentui/*` out of the bundle;
`--format=esm` preserves `"type": "module"`. After building, `npm run check` must pass and `npm test`
must stay green. Restart OpenCode to load the new bundle into memory.

## 9. Security

See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) for the formal responsible-disclosure policy, supported versions,
response targets and the **package lineage** register.

### Package lineage (`@opencode/plugin` vs `@opencode-ai/plugin`)

Both packages are legitimate and are used for different SDK generations. `@opencode-ai/plugin` (and
`@opencode-ai/sdk`) are the official v1 namespace; `@opencode/plugin` is the v2 plugin SDK maintained by
**Dax Raad (`thdxr`)**, the creator and architect of OpenCode. The runtime imports `Plugin` from
`@opencode/plugin` and keeps the v1 `server()` export for dual compatibility. `@opencode/plugin` is
pinned to an exact version (`2.0.16`) and `package-lock.json` carries its registry URL and `sha512`
integrity hash, so `npm ci` is byte-identical. Verify with:

```bash
npm ls @opencode/plugin @opencode-ai/plugin @opencode-ai/sdk
npm view @opencode/plugin version maintainers   # → thdxr <d@ironbay.co>
npm audit --omit=dev   # 0 vulnerabilities
```

The coexistence of the two scopes is therefore not typosquatting: it is the documented v1/v2 plugin
surface, all installed from the public npm registry.

Operational defaults that matter:

- The dashboard binds to loopback (`127.0.0.1`) and enforces a Host/Origin gate against DNS rebinding.
- State lives in a local SQLite database; the host session store is opened **read-only**.
- Credentials are never stored by the runtime — model access uses the host's own provider configuration.
- Teammates are spawned with an integrity deny-list of tools (`team_create`, `team_cleanup`, `team_merge`,
  `team_shutdown`, `task`, `todowrite`), extendable through `deniedTools`.

## 10. Provenance and license

- Derived from `@hueyexe/opencode-ensemble@0.18.0` (MIT): `src/`, `dist/`, `LICENSE` and the social
  preview image originate there.
- `package.json` was rewritten only in `name`, `version`, `description`, `repository`, `keywords`,
  `files`, `scripts` (`test`, `check`, `typecheck`, `build`) and the `exports`/`types` map. Since `0.18.2`
  the package root resolves through `exports["."]` to the compiled `dist/index.js` (with
  `exports["."].types` → `src/index.ts`), so plain Node consumers no longer hit TypeScript syntax. The
  optional `./rpc` and `./tui` companion subpaths still point at their TypeScript sources and require
  Bun/Node type-stripping.
- `@opencode/plugin` (`2.0.16`) is pinned by exact version in `dependencies`, ahead of the upstream
  `@opencode/plugin@2.0.3`; its runtime/tooling dependencies are pinned through `package-lock.json`.
- The published upstream tarball omitted `tsconfig.json`; the file versioned here was recovered from the
  upstream repository with unchanged compiler settings.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

_Nothing yet._

## [0.18.3] - 2026-10-27

Runtime hardening batch on top of `0.18.2`: hiring hygiene at spawn time, a partitioned auto-commit
ledger, published exports that never leak TypeScript, and a CI matrix pinned to Node versions that can
actually run the deterministic suite. The runtime entrypoints (`dist/index.js`, `dist/rpc.js`,
`dist/tui.js`) are rebuilt from `src/` and validated against the **60** deterministic suites, zero mocks.

### Added

- **Deterministic Persona Gap hook in `team_spawn`** (TICKET-HARNESS-77). Spawning an agent whose
  `build` / `plan` / `general` / unknown type does not match an official persona now yields a
  `[PERSONA GAP ALERT]` banner in the `team_spawn` return demanding an explicit vacancy specification,
  plus orienting notes in `team_status` and `team_cleanup`. The baseline classification lives in-code
  (independent of `HOME`), so a missing user config cannot silence the alert.
- **Per-card auto-commit ledger** (TICKET-HARNESS-82). Migration 21 adds a nullable `task_id` to
  `team_modified_file`; `recordModifiedFile` / `listModifiedFiles(taskId)` filter strictly by card and
  the completion hook commits surgically with a lean message (≤100 chars). Legacy v20 databases upgrade
  in place, and files recorded without a card keep the previous safe fallback.
- **Regression coverage for the batch**: `tests/test_ticket_harness_77_persona_gap.mjs`,
  `tests/test_ticket_harness_82_ledger_partition.mjs`,
  `tests/test_ticket_harness_87_exports.mjs` and `tests/test_ticket_harness_89_node_pins.mjs`,
  bringing the runner (`tests/run_all.mjs`) to **60 suites**.

### Changed

- **Published `exports` sanitized** (TICKET-HARNESS-87). The root entry resolves to `dist/index.js`
  through a real `import.meta.resolve` probe, and the `./rpc` / `./tui` subpaths now resolve to
  `dist/rpc.js` / `dist/tui.js` instead of raw TypeScript. No runtime condition exposes `.ts`/`.tsx`;
  `node --check` passes for all three bundles and the `files` allowlist ships exactly the compiled
  runtime targets.
- **Robust `HOME` fallback** (TICKET-HARNESS-87, `ensemble.ts`). `isUsableHome` now rejects relative and
  empty candidates — including the literal `"~"` / `"~/sub"` — and accepts absolute paths only, so a
  subprocess without `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` never resolves data under `./~`.
- **Node pins hardened in CI** (TICKET-HARNESS-89). `ci.yml` pins the matrix to `22.23.4` and `24.22.1`
  with `check-latest`, `publish.yml` runs on `22.23.4`, and the composite `setup-bun` action pins
  `24.22.1` instead of a floating tag. A real `Bun.YAML` verifier plus a mutation proof (floating pin /
  vulnerable version) guards the contract.
- **Package version** bumped to `0.18.3`, with `package-lock.json` kept in lockstep at the root and
  package entries.

### Fixed

- **Hermetic CI runner for the SDET block** (`tests/test_bloco_c_sdet_harness_87_89.mjs`). The suite now
  degrades gracefully to `SKIP` when the sibling `opencode_repo` checkout or the `bun` binary is absent,
  instead of failing the whole run for environment reasons; the deterministic checks still execute
  whenever both are available.

## [0.18.2] - 2026-10-20

Release-governance patch on top of `0.18.1`: the runtime code is unchanged, but the **published
artifact** is now correct for plain Node consumers, the dependency tree is audited and the package
lineage is documented. Everything shipped by TICKET-RELEASE-01 through TICKET-RELEASE-06 is recorded
here, because those changes landed after the `0.18.1` tag.

### Added

- **Conditional `exports` map with a compiled runtime target.** `exports["."]` now resolves through
  `"types": "./src/index.ts"` and `"default": "./dist/index.js"`, so a regular Node consumer importing
  `ensemble-room-lowcost` loads the ESM bundle instead of failing with a TypeScript syntax error. The
  top-level `"types"` field was added for editors that do not read conditional exports, and the legacy
  `"module"` field now points at the same compiled bundle so bundlers that ignore `exports` no longer
  receive TypeScript either.

## [0.18.1] - 2026-10-20

Hardening release over the upstream base `@hueyexe/opencode-ensemble@0.18.0`. The theme is
**token-efficient orchestration without behavioural regressions**: teammates are born idle, the lead
sleeps, and the schema survives the upgrade.

### Added

- **Native standby spawn.** `team_spawn` accepts `standby: true`, registering the member without sending
  an init prompt. The full prompt is persisted in `team_member.spawn_context` and delivered by the first
  `team_message` / `team_broadcast` addressed to that member. Spawning costs zero tokens.
- **Idempotent wake guard.** The `standby → starting` transition is a guarded
  `UPDATE … WHERE execution_status = 'standby'`, so concurrent messages cannot duplicate the init prompt.
  On transport failure the member is reverted to `standby` and the stored context is replayed on retry.
- **`silentLead` configuration flag** (default `true`). Lead-bound messages are persisted in SQLite
  (`delivered = 0`) instead of firing `promptAsync`; `buildLeadSystemPrompt` injects the backlog on the
  lead's next legitimate turn and marks it delivered. Set to `false` to restore the legacy per-message wake.
- **Systematic board waker.** `team_tasks_complete` wakes the lead exactly once when
  `total > 0 && completed === total` with a synthetic `[System: All team tasks completed on board]`
  message. This is the single automatic lead-wake event.
- **Per-agent model fallback chains** (`fallbackModelsByAgent`) with base-persona symmetry, so
  multi-instance agents inherit the chain declared for their base role.
- **Primary/secondary compaction awareness.** `isSessionCompacting()` exposes
  `session.time_compacting > 0` as the immunity signal used by the watchdog.
- **`deniedTools` configuration key** to extend the built-in teammate tool deny-list per ecosystem,
  unioned additively across global and project scopes.
- **`roomInactivityThresholdMs` and `roomInactivityCheckMs`** configuration keys, decoupling the
  inactivity threshold from the sweep cadence.
- **Dashboard HTTP API:** `/`, `/api/state`, `/api/health`, `/api/session/:id/activity` and
  `/api/chat/send`, bound to `127.0.0.1` with a Host/Origin gate against DNS rebinding.
- **Intra-card handover** (`team_task_handover`) for sequential bench partnerships on the same card:
  atomic reassignment, wake with handover notes, and automatic standby for the sender.
- **Public documentation:** this changelog, `SECURITY.md`, and a sanitized `README.md` covering
  architecture, the five hardening layers, the full configuration catalog and troubleshooting.

### Changed

- **Hook shielding.** `shouldNudgeIdleMember` no longer nudges members in `standby`, and
  `shouldAlarmFastIdle` no longer raises a false "agent died" alarm for them. The predicates are exported
  seams without decision changes.
- **Watchdog heartbeat.** Stale members that show real progress (`ProgressTracker`: steps and output
  tokens above `stallTokenThreshold`) have `time_updated` renewed instead of being aborted.
- **Migration 12.** `team_member` is rebuilt with an updated `CHECK` constraint that accepts `standby`,
  carrying every column added by Migrations 3–11 and recreating both indexes. The migration runs inside a
  single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction tracked by `PRAGMA user_version`, making it atomic and idempotent.
- **`#default` variant sentinel.** `model.variant === "default"` is normalized away at parse and format
  time, preventing an unmatchable `provider/model#default` key that used to restart the fallback chain on
  every retry.
- **Fallback precedence** is explicit: exact agent key → base-persona key → global chain → legacy
  `modelFallback` → built-in default. Chains are never empty; malformed entries are discarded and
  duplicates collapse.
- **Failover de-duplication.** A per-`teamId:memberName` cooldown (`FAILOVER_COOLDOWN_MS`, 10 minutes)
  collapses a 429 burst into a single chain advance.
- **Zero-noise failover.** Switched and suppressed decisions only log and update `team_member.model`;
  chain exhaustion is silent as well (log + cooldown, no lead notification). The single automatic lead
  wake is the systematic full-board closure event.
- **Conditional prompt coercion.** With `silentLead` active, the mandatory "report to the lead before
  stopping" directive is replaced by a collaboration directive. Legacy text is preserved verbatim when the
  flag is off.
- **Hermetic tests.** The host session store is no longer a prerequisite; the `session` DDL is versioned
  in `tests/fixtures/session_schema.sql` and applied to a throwaway database under `.test-scratch/`.
- **`package.json` `files`** now publishes `CHANGELOG.md` and `SECURITY.md` alongside `dist`, `src`,
  `tsconfig.json`, `LICENSE`, `README.md` and the social preview image.

### Fixed

- Standby members no longer receive idle nudges or fast-idle alarms.
- Sessions in context compaction are no longer aborted as stale after the TTL.
- The runtime propagates the explicit `agent` on every `promptAsync` relaunch (member, isolated session and
  lead), so the host cannot reset `session.agent` to its default.
- Task without an `assignee` is atomically assigned to its author on completion, keeping the board honest.
- Wake transport failures are absorbed by `.catch` — zero `unhandledRejection`.

### Deprecated

- `modelFallback` remains supported for backward compatibility but is superseded by `fallbackModels` and
  `fallbackModelsByAgent`.
- `Watchdog.stop()` is retained as a legacy alias of `dispose()`.

### Security

- Dashboard binds to `127.0.0.1` and validates `Host`/`Origin` on both `GET` and `POST`.
- The host session store is opened read-only; the runtime never writes to it.
- See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) for the disclosure policy.

### Tests

- 48 deterministic suites, thousands of assertions, zero mocks, executed against both the real bundle
  (`dist/index.js`) and the `.ts` sources of `src/`.

# Security Policy

## Supported versions

| Version | Supported |
|---|---|
| `0.18.3` (current) | Yes — security fixes are released on this line |
| `0.18.x` | Yes — previous patches remain installable, but fixes land on `0.18.3` |
| `< 0.18.0` | No |

Only the latest patch of the supported minor line receives security fixes. Upgrading is always the
recommended remediation.

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Please do not open a public issue for a security problem.**

Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting on this repository:

1. Go to the **Security** tab of `github.com/maiteuxzanela/ensemble-room-lowcost`.
2. Click **Report a vulnerability**.
3. Describe the issue with enough detail to reproduce it.

A good report includes:

- Affected version (`package.json` value or bundle commit).
- The affected component: plugin runtime (`dist/index.js`), source (`src/`), dashboard HTTP server,
  SQLite migration path, or the messaging/wake pipeline.
- Reproduction steps or a minimal proof of concept.
- Observed impact and the preconditions an attacker needs.
- Whether the issue also affects the upstream base `@hueyexe/opencode-ensemble@0.18.0`.

Do not include real credentials, provider API keys or production data in the report. Redact them.

## Response targets

| Stage | Target |
|---|---|
| Acknowledgement of the report | within 72 hours |
| Initial triage and severity assessment | within 7 calendar days |
| Fix or documented mitigation for critical/high issues | within 30 calendar days |
| Coordinated public disclosure | after a fix is available, by mutual agreement |

These are targets, not contractual guarantees. If a fix requires coordination with the upstream project
or an affected provider, the timeline will be communicated in the report thread.

## Scope

In scope:

- The plugin runtime and its distributed bundle (`dist/index.js`).
- The local dashboard HTTP server (binding, Host/Origin validation, endpoint authorization, input
  handling).
- SQLite schema and migration logic (`src/schema.ts`), including upgrade paths that could corrupt or
  leak data.
- The wake and messaging pipeline: standby wake guards, silent lead delivery, message durability.
- Model fallback resolution, including any path that could leak selectors, credentials or session
  identifiers.
- Tool deny-list enforcement for spawned teammates.

Out of scope:

- Vulnerabilities in OpenCode itself, in a model provider, or in a third-party package — report those
  upstream. We will still relay a report when it is directly relevant.
- Issues that require an already-compromised host account, root access, or physical access.
- Social-engineering scenarios against operators.
- Denial of service caused by deliberately oversized local configuration files.
- Findings that only affect unsupported versions.

## Package lineage and supply-chain provenance

An external release audit flagged the coexistence of `@opencode/plugin` and `@opencode-ai/plugin` as a
possible typosquatting / supply-chain risk. It is not. Both namespaces are legitimate and have different
owners and purposes:

| Package | Role | Lineage |
|---|---|---|
| `@opencode-ai/plugin` | v1 plugin/tool SDK (`tool`, `Plugin` types) | OpenCode official SDK namespace, used here for tool definitions and types |
| `@opencode-ai/sdk` | v1 server/client SDK (`OpencodeClient`) | Same official namespace |
| `@opencode/plugin` | v2 plugin SDK: `Plugin` from the root, `Rpc` from `@opencode/plugin/rpc`, TUI helpers from `@opencode/plugin/tui` | Maintained by **Dax Raad (`thdxr`)**, creator and architect of OpenCode |

How the runtime uses them:

- `src/index.ts` imports `Plugin` from `@opencode/plugin` and also re-exports the legacy `server()` shape
  from `@opencode-ai/plugin` (dual V1/V2 compatibility, upstream issue #36).
- `src/rpc.ts` imports `Rpc` from `@opencode/plugin/rpc`; `src/tui.tsx` imports `Plugin` from
  `@opencode/plugin/tui`. Both are companion entrypoints and are optional at runtime.

Verification properties that make the dependency auditable:

- `@opencode/plugin` is pinned to an **exact version** (`2.0.16`) — no `^`, `~` or `latest` range — and
  `package-lock.json` records the `registry.npmjs.org` tarball plus its `sha512` integrity hash.
  `npm ci` therefore installs byte-identical code.
- The package is published on the public npm registry under the `@opencode` scope with the same maintainer
  as OpenCode itself; it is not an unowned, look-alike name.
- `npm audit --omit=dev` reports **0 vulnerabilities** for the runtime dependency tree.
- `@opencode/plugin`, `@opencode-ai/plugin` and `@opencode-ai/sdk` are declared as regular
  `dependencies` (not post-install hooks, not git URLs, not tarball URLs); no package in the runtime tree
  prompts for credentials or installs from a non-registry source.

To audit the claim yourself:

```bash
npm ls @opencode/plugin @opencode-ai/plugin @opencode-ai/sdk
npm view @opencode/plugin version maintainers   # → maintainer: thdxr <d@ironbay.co>
npm audit --omit=dev
```

If a future release needs a different package from the `@opencode*` families, it must be added by an
explicit, reviewed change to `package.json` with an exact version and a lockfile diff — never as a
transitive surprise.

## Secure operating assumptions

The runtime is designed as a **local, single-operator** tool:

- The dashboard binds to loopback (`127.0.0.1`) and rejects requests whose `Host`/`Origin` do not match.
  Exposing it behind a reverse proxy without preserving the original `Host` header is unsupported.
- The host session store (`opencode.db`) is opened **read-only**. The runtime must never need write
  access to it.
- The runtime stores no provider credentials. Model access is delegated to the host's own provider
  configuration; keep that configuration outside the repository.
- Spawned teammates receive an integrity deny-list (`team_create`, `team_cleanup`, `team_merge`,
  `team_shutdown`, `task`, `todowrite`), optionally extended through the `deniedTools` configuration key.
  Denial is additive across scopes: a project file can never re-enable a globally denied tool.
- Multi-agent orchestration implies executing tool calls requested by models. Treat any untrusted
  repository content as potential prompt-injection input and keep human review on destructive operations
  (commits, pushes, merges, shutdowns).

## Disclosure policy

We follow coordinated disclosure. Once a fix is released, we publish an advisory describing the issue,
the affected versions and the remediation, and credit the reporter unless anonymity is requested.

## Security-relevant configuration checklist

When operating the runtime, verify:

- [ ] `dashboardPort` is either `0` (disabled) or reachable only from loopback.
- [ ] No `ensemble.json` in a shared repository contains internal hostnames, tokens or provider secrets.
- [ ] `deniedTools` covers ecosystem-specific tools that must never be available to workers.
- [ ] The plugin version pinned in `opencode.json` is the supported line (`0.18.x`).
- [ ] Local commits produced by the runtime are reviewed before any push to a remote.
